plain_language.what_did_we_find: Validation now runs against a detached exact-commit snapshot instead of the mutable publication worktree. Publication is refused when any declared publication input no longer matches that snapshot. Stage-specific content dependencies reuse the costly suite after a publication-only document change and rerun it after a real test dependency change. Thirty-one focused controls pass; four failed ordered closure attempts are preserved and repaired. No scientific experiment ran.
plain_language.is_it_interesting: Yes. The repair closes an edit-and-restore contamination path while avoiding needless suite invalidation from global HEAD changes that do not affect the suite.
plain_language.does_it_require_more_work: No further repair follows from the passing ordered closure. The next separate item is the read-only audit of eighteen historical short-process memory receipts.

controls.validation_snapshot: A detached worktree at the bound commit supplies every tracked validation byte; current publication-worktree edits cannot change suite inputs.
controls.publication_match: Every declared publication dependency is content-compared after validation and after refresh/final checks.
controls.stage_dependencies: Status, suite and publication stages bind separate exact file sets without using the global commit identity in their reusable content digest.
controls.fail_closed: Incomplete dependency sets, unsafe cached outputs, changed cached bytes, publication mismatch, linked source ancestry and failed commands stop closure.
controls.historical_preservation: The frozen lib/closure_controls.py and all historical scientific artifacts remain unchanged.

coverage: immutable host-payload cloning and changed-payload refusal
ordinary source ancestry and narrow payload hydration
snapshot-local receipt relocation, unrelated-root preservation, interruption/resume, exclusive ownership and cache tamper refusal
